title: Retro - Enterprise escalation follow-up (streaming disconnects / comms + metadata gaps)
summary: Team retro on a recent enterprise escalation involving intermittent streaming disconnects and elevated timeouts for a Dedicated customer. Main gaps: missing request metadata in the initial ticket (request IDs, model pin/version, region/POP, SDK version, connect timeout vs read timeout), lack of a single dashboard view Support can use, and workaround guidance that was either too vague or scattered across threads. Agreed to tighten escalation required fields, add a Support-facing dashboard panel + runbook link, and publish a validated known-issues page with safe-to-share reconnect guidance and a clear decision tree (client retry vs region failover vs model rollback).
topics: Support intake quality: required fields, request IDs, SDK + timeout settings
Dedicated vs Hosted routing confusion (which metrics to check first)
Dashboards: streaming disconnect rate, gateway 499/504, regional breakdown
Validated workarounds vs speculation; what is safe to share
Comms cadence and expectations for enterprise accounts
Handoff to SRE / incident declaration thresholds and paging hygiene
next_steps: Support to adopt a stricter escalation template (request IDs, region, model version, SDK version, timeout settings, reproduction window).
SRE to add a Support-friendly dashboard view for streaming disconnect rate + correlated timeout/5xx panels with runbook links.
Priya + Owen to draft/publish known-issues page for streaming disconnects with a validated workaround decision tree and safe-to-share snippets.
Dev + Rachel to align on enterprise comms update cadence template (every 30–60 min during active mitigation; otherwise hourly).
Rafael to propose a paging threshold policy for “enterprise-impacting but not global” issues to avoid premature incident declaration.
action_items: Owen Phillips — Update Support escalation required fields checklist (include request_id(s), org/project, region, model+version, SDK version, timeout values, streaming mode, sample curl/SDK snippet) — Due 2026-02-23
Priya Shah — Draft Known Issue: Streaming disconnects & reconnect guidance; include decision tree and log fields to request; route to Docs for safe-to-share review — Due 2026-02-25
Rafael Mendes — Create/refresh dashboard panel: streaming_disconnect_rate by region/model + correlate with gateway 499/504 and runtime queue depth; add runbook link — Due 2026-02-26
Sean Gallagher — Clarify incident vs escalation criteria for enterprise-only impact; propose a 2-week pilot and measure page volume — Due 2026-03-01
Rachel Kim — Write comms macro for enterprise escalations (investigation started / mitigation applied / monitoring / RCA) and circulate to CS — Due 2026-02-24
Dev Patel — Schedule 30-min training segment in Support standup on new escalation template + where to find dashboard/known-issues page — Due 2026-02-27
transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Title: Retro - Enterprise escalation follow-up (streaming disconnects / comms + metadata gaps)
Date: Feb 18, 2026
Time: 5:00pm - 5:48pm PT
Duration: 48 minutes

Attendees:
- Dev Patel (Director, Customer Support)
- Rachel Kim (Enterprise CS alignment)
- Liam O'Rourke (TAM)
- Owen Phillips (Support Eng)
- Priya Shah (Known-issues triage)
- Rafael Mendes (SRE Oncall / escalation)
- Sean Gallagher (Director of SRE)

Auto-generated summary (Fireflies):
- Discussed escalation timeline, missing metadata and delays.
- Identified dashboard gaps and agreed on a Support-facing view.
- Agreed on validated customer-safe workarounds and a known-issues page.
- Clarified comms cadence and incident thresholds.


00:00 Dev Patel: Alright, thanks everyone. This is the retro for the enterprise escalation from last week, the streaming disconnects and then the sort of cascading timeouts. Goal is not blame. It’s like, what slowed us down, what do we fix in the playbook.

00:22 Rachel Kim: Yeah and from CS side, the customer basically felt like we were asking for the same info three times, and they didn’t know if they should fail over regions or just keep retrying.

00:32 Liam O'Rourke: Also they escalated to their VP pretty quickly, because their app had like live chat, so streaming drops are super visible.

00:44 Dev Patel: Yep. Owen, can you do the quick timeline? Like what came in on the ticket.

00:49 Owen Phillips: Sure. So initial message from customer was “stream terminates mid-response” and they pasted two timestamps, but no request IDs. It was Dedicated in us-east, pinned model, I think… I want to say “Llama 3.1 70B” but I’m not 100%—

01:06 Priya Shah: I think it was the “70B instruct” variant, but yeah, the exact version wasn’t in the first note.

01:13 Owen Phillips: Right. We asked for request IDs. They sent like one, then later three more, but not the failed ones. And the SDK version, we didn’t ask until like, later. That’s on us.

01:28 Rafael Mendes: On the SRE side, once we got the request ID we could correlate, but it took too long to get the right set. Also we were missing “region + POP” vs just “us-east”. There’s multiple edges.

01:41 Sean Gallagher: Yeah and I’ll say we got paged pretty quickly, but the page itself didn’t have enough to do anything. It was basically “enterprise customer upset, streaming broken”. Which is… valid emotionally, but not a page payload.

01:55 Dev Patel: Exactly the kind of thing we want to fix with required fields. Rachel, what did the customer ask for specifically?

02:02 Rachel Kim: Two things. One, do they need to change anything in their client reconnect. Two, can we guarantee this won’t happen again, which obviously we can’t, but they wanted confidence.

02:15 Liam O'Rourke: And they asked if it’s a Redwood issue or their load balancer. They have some proxy in front; I forgot which.

02:22 Owen Phillips: Yeah they mentioned Envoy, but I’m not sure. That might have been me hearing “envoy” when they said “our envoy thing”.

02:31 Dev Patel: Okay. So gaps: request metadata intake. Let’s list what we didn’t capture early.

02:37 Priya Shah: Request IDs plural, with success and failure examples. Also: SDK language and version. They were using Python but the exact version matters because retry behavior changed recently.

02:49 Owen Phillips: Timeout settings. We asked “what’s your timeout” and they said “30 seconds” but that could be connect timeout or read timeout, and for streaming you can have different semantics. We didn’t ask the precise config.

03:05 Rafael Mendes: And whether they’re using HTTP/2, or proxies that do idle timeouts. A lot of streaming disconnects are idle timeout at some layer. If they have a 15s idle timeout and tokens pause, you get a cut.

03:18 Sean Gallagher: Also, we didn’t get “model version pinned” vs “alias”. The runtime behavior can differ slightly across patch versions.

03:27 Dev Patel: So support template should force those. We already have a draft of required fields, but we should be explicit: request_id(s), org/project, region, model+version, SDK version, timeout values, streaming mode, and reproduction window.

03:44 Rachel Kim: And impact. Like percentage of sessions affected. They said “a lot” and later it was like 5-10% of streams.

03:52 Liam O'Rourke: Yeah and the TAM thing is: if it’s 5% but it’s their top workflow, it’s effectively 100% impactful. So we need both, like frequency and business impact.

04:07 Dev Patel: Great. Next: dashboards. Rafael, you said there wasn’t a single view Support could look at.

04:13 Rafael Mendes: Correct. There’s a bunch of SRE dashboards, but they’re not “Support safe”. They’re like 30 panels, internal naming. Support needs a simple entrypoint: streaming disconnect rate by region/model, plus correlated gateway 499/504, plus runtime queue depth or token generation stalls.

04:31 Owen Phillips: Right now we were screenshotting from three different places, and I was basically copying graphs into Slack, which is not great.

04:38 Priya Shah: And we didn’t know if we should treat it as gateway vs runtime vs customer network, because it’s all “disconnect”.

04:46 Sean Gallagher: Exactly. The disconnect metric needs attribution buckets: client disconnect, upstream timeout, server close, gateway close. Even if the attribution is imperfect.

04:58 Rafael Mendes: We do have some of that in logs but not surfaced as a metric. At least in the short term, we can do a “proxy metric”: 499-ish (client closed request) and 504-ish (gateway timeout). That helps separate.

05:12 Dev Patel: Okay. Let’s talk workarounds and docs. Priya, what’s the current state.

05:18 Priya Shah: We have some guidance in Slack threads and like an old internal doc, but it’s not a curated known-issues page. Also some guidance is speculative, like “try increasing keepalive” but we never validated with the runtime team.

05:34 Rachel Kim: That was a big issue. CS asked “what can I tell them” and we were like “maybe increase timeout” which is not a great enterprise answer.

05:42 Sean Gallagher: If it’s not validated, don’t ship it as a workaround. I’d rather we say “we’re investigating, here are the logs to capture” than random knob-turning.

05:52 Owen Phillips: Agree. But we also need something practical. Like, reconnect patterns for streaming, idempotency guidance, and recommended backoff. That’s safe.

06:04 Rafael Mendes: And also region failover guidance, but only when we have evidence it’s regional. In this case we thought it was “us-east only” but we didn’t check eu-west or us-west because it was Dedicated, so…

06:18 Liam O'Rourke: They asked “can we fail over to hosted temporarily” and we didn’t have an answer.

06:23 Dev Patel: For Dedicated, the policy is: if they have a fallback policy configured, yes, but otherwise no. That’s a product question, but we can at least document the standard options: retry, reconnect, increase read timeout, pin model version rollback, and if we declare incident then we can recommend region shift if available.

06:44 Priya Shah: I can draft a decision tree: Step 1 confirm disconnect type (client closed vs server) using request_id and status codes. Step 2 if it correlates with gateway timeouts, adjust read timeout and retry with jitter. Step 3 if it correlates with runtime queue depth, consider batching/throughput and dedicated autoscale. Step 4 if it correlates with a specific model version, roll back or repin.

07:08 Sean Gallagher: That’s good. Just be careful: “roll back model” for enterprise needs an approval step. We don’t want Support telling them to randomly switch without us confirming compatibility.

07:18 Priya Shah: Yep, we can tag as “requires Redwood confirmation” vs “safe to share”.

07:24 Dev Patel: Great. Comms. Rachel, what went wrong.

07:29 Rachel Kim: We had no steady cadence. Support posted one update, then 90 minutes of silence while everyone was in graphs. Customer got anxious. Even if we don’t have an answer, we need: “investigation ongoing, next update by X time.”

07:46 Liam O'Rourke: They literally said “are you still working on it”.

07:49 Owen Phillips: We were working. We just didn’t send messages.

07:52 Dev Patel: So we need a macro. Like every 30-60 minutes during active mitigation for enterprise.

08:01 Sean Gallagher: Align with incident comms. If SRE is running it as an incident, we can mirror. If it’s not an incident, Support still needs a cadence. But don’t promise an RCA timeline unless we can do it.

08:16 Rafael Mendes: Also it matters if we’re paging. If I’m oncall and getting pings in Slack plus pages, it’s messy. We should have one thread, ideally #incidents if it meets criteria.

08:29 Dev Patel: On that: was this an incident?

08:32 Rafael Mendes: It was enterprise-only, single dedicated cluster. We didn’t see global. So by our current criteria, no. But Support asked to declare because of comms structure.

08:43 Sean Gallagher: We should not declare incidents just for comms. We can have an “incident-adjacent” escalation workflow with comms templates without full incident overhead.

08:53 Rachel Kim: But enterprise customers like the structure of incident updates.

08:57 Sean Gallagher: I get it. We can do structured updates without incident declaration. Just don’t page the whole world.

09:07 Dev Patel: So action item: define “enterprise escalation comms mode” with set cadence, without incident.

09:15 Priya Shah: And make it super clear in the playbook: what triggers SRE page vs what is a support escalation only.

09:23 Rafael Mendes: Yes. For paging thresholds: if disconnect rate above X% for Y minutes, and impacting multiple customers or multiple regions, page. If single customer and we have logs, maybe it’s a Slack consult first.

09:39 Owen Phillips: The problem is “enterprise customer upset” is hard to encode.

09:43 Dev Patel: True, but we can define “enterprise + production down” as page, and “enterprise + partial degradation” as consult, unless it crosses a numeric threshold.

09:56 Liam O'Rourke: Also consider their business hours. They’re east coast, so our delay felt worse.

10:02 Dev Patel: Okay. Let’s dig into the specific metadata that would have cut time. Owen, what would have made it faster.

10:09 Owen Phillips: If we’d asked for: five request IDs that failed, five that succeeded, all within a 15 minute window. Plus their client config snippet and SDK version. And the model+version. We could have given Rafael the set immediately.

10:28 Rafael Mendes: Also the “x-redwood-request-id” header vs their own trace ID. They were sending their own “request id” but it wasn’t ours.

10:37 Priya Shah: Oh yeah. That was confusing. We said “request id” and they sent their app’s uuid. So we need to explicitly say “Redwood request_id from response headers or error body”.

10:50 Dev Patel: That’s huge. Add exact instructions + screenshot. And we should add in the SDK how to log it.

11:00 Sean Gallagher: The SDK PR is in flight, right?

11:03 Owen Phillips: Monica and Ibrahim are doing it. But for now we can document: in Python, log `e.request_id` or whatever it is, if present.

11:14 Priya Shah: I’ll confirm exact field names; I don’t want to publish wrong.

11:18 Dev Patel: Great. Dashboards again: we need something Support can access and understand. Rafael, can you deliver a v1 by next week?

11:26 Rafael Mendes: Yeah. I can do a “Support Escalation - Streaming” dashboard: disconnect rate, timeouts, 5xx, by region/model, and link to the runbook.

11:38 Sean Gallagher: Make sure it has a “how to read this” blurb. Otherwise people will stare at it.

11:44 Owen Phillips: Please. Because I was staring at “kv cache eviction” graphs like, what am I supposed to do with that.

11:51 (crosstalk)

11:52 Dev Patel: Okay, and known-issues page. Priya, can you outline what sections it needs.

11:58 Priya Shah: Yup: Symptoms (what customer sees), Common causes (client idle timeout, proxy, read timeout, server close), Triage checklist (what to collect: request IDs, region, SDK version, timeout settings, sample code, timestamps), Workarounds (validated): recommended retry/backoff, reconnect behavior, increase read timeout, disable overly aggressive proxy idle timeout, and when to consider model repin or region change (requires Redwood confirmation). Then “Internal diagnostics” section: which dashboards, logs, what to check in runtime.

12:33 Rachel Kim: Also a “what we can say” section. Like safe-to-share wording.

12:38 Priya Shah: Yes, we can add “Customer-facing guidance” subsection.

12:43 Sean Gallagher: Please keep anything about internal capacity, noisy neighbor, etc. internal-only. Customers interpret that badly.

12:51 Liam O'Rourke: They already asked if they were sharing GPUs with someone else.

12:55 Dev Patel: And the answer is “Dedicated is isolated”, but there are still shared upstream components sometimes. That’s nuance.

13:02 Rafael Mendes: For Dedicated, the gateway can still be shared depending on setup. But we don’t want to debate architecture in an escalation.

13:10 Dev Patel: Exactly. Comms templates should avoid deep infra speculation.

13:15 Rachel Kim: Another thing: We didn’t have a single owner on the thread. Customer got messages from me, from Support, from SRE, it was confusing.

13:25 Dev Patel: Good point. For enterprise escalations, we should designate a “customer comms owner” (CSM/TAM) and a “technical incident lead”. Support can coordinate but not all talk.

13:38 Owen Phillips: And we should stop asking the customer the same questions. One intake doc.

13:42 Dev Patel: That’s where the template helps. Also the incident-bot automation—Miles is building it. It’ll prompt for required fields.

13:52 Rafael Mendes: The bot should also create one thread and pin the “next update by” time.

13:58 Dev Patel: I’ll relay. For now, manual.

14:03 Sean Gallagher: Can we talk about why streaming disconnects are so hard? It’s multi-layer. So the runbook should emphasize: we need to distinguish “server terminated stream” vs “client / proxy terminated.” Otherwise we chase ghosts.

14:17 Priya Shah: We should include examples of error messages. Like “unexpected EOF”, “connection reset by peer”, etc.

14:23 Owen Phillips: Right and in Python requests it can show as “ChunkedEncodingError” which is not obvious.

14:30 Rachel Kim: Is it okay to tell them to implement reconnect? Some customers assume streaming is one connection only.

14:36 Sean Gallagher: It is okay to recommend reconnect, with idempotency caveats. But we need to be careful on “duplicate output”. If they reconnect mid-generation, they can get repeated tokens.

14:48 Rafael Mendes: We can recommend they send the conversation history and use a deterministic seed if supported, but not all models support that. Keep it general: treat streaming as best-effort, implement resume by re-request with context.

15:03 Dev Patel: Put it in the doc as “recommended pattern”.

15:07 Priya Shah: Will do.

15:10 Dev Patel: Any other gaps? Liam?

15:13 Liam O'Rourke: We didn’t have a clear statement on after-hours for Dedicated. They asked “do you have 24/7” and we said “SRE oncall” but Support after-hours is limited. So messaging was confusing.

15:27 Rachel Kim: Yep. We need SLA language by tier. Otherwise it’s ad hoc.

15:33 Dev Patel: That’s in the playbook v2 workstream, but we should feed this example into it.

15:38 Sean Gallagher: Also, paging hygiene. Don’t page SRE for “need update for customer”. Page for “service down, need mitigation.”

15:47 Dev Patel: Agreed.

16:00 Dev Patel: Okay, let’s capture action items. Owen: update required fields checklist and include explicit “Redwood request_id” instructions.

16:08 Owen Phillips: Yep. I’ll do it. And I’ll add “five failed + five success” guidance.

16:14 Dev Patel: Priya: draft known-issues page with safe-to-share + internal diagnostics.

16:18 Priya Shah: Yes, and I’ll route to Elliot’s team for wording, but I can own the first draft.

16:24 Dev Patel: Rafael: dashboard v1 + runbook link.

16:27 Rafael Mendes: Yep. I’ll build a simple one and share it in #support.

16:33 Dev Patel: Sean: clarify incident vs escalation criteria for enterprise-only and propose pilot.

16:39 Sean Gallagher: I’ll write a short policy and we can try it for two weeks, measure page volume.

16:45 Dev Patel: Rachel: comms macro + cadence.

16:48 Rachel Kim: I’ll draft. Include “next update by” line.

16:52 Dev Patel: Great. Anything else before we close?

16:56 Owen Phillips: One more: the customer compared us to OpenAI, saying they rarely see streaming drops. We should be ready to explain that network conditions differ and they should still implement retries.

17:08 Sean Gallagher: Yep. And Bedrock too, same. Everyone has disconnects; they just don’t talk about it.

17:14 Dev Patel: Okay. Thanks all. I’ll post notes and link the action items. Meeting adjourned.

(End of transcript)
